ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against Canada's Sanctions List (Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act), OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Canadian Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre (FINTRAC) guidance. Enhanced due diligence is required for all Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), including domestic and foreign PEPs and their family members and close associates, in accordance with PCMLTFA obligations. Beneficial ownership must be verified to the 25% threshold, with ongoing transaction monitoring and re-screening at formation, upon any partnership interest change, and before establishing Swift LC or TT Wire payment rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) via NUANS name search through authorized service providers
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be in Latin characters and comprised of English or French words. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated phonetically into the Latin alphabet. The legal element of a limited partnership must be expressed as 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.' or 'LP'. Names must be distinguishable from existing registered names, reserved names, and relevant trademarks under the Alberta Partnership Act and the provincial name-guidelines.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of a name rejection, the applicant may file an administrative review request with Service Alberta Corporate Registry, attaching the rejection letter, a newly generated NUANS report with alternative names, and written distinguishability arguments. If the administrative review is unsuccessful, the applicant may appeal to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review. No statutory fee is charged for the first administrative review; an authorized service provider may levy a resubmission fee for a fresh NUANS search.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible as a registered office in Alberta provided it offers a physical street address in Alberta, accepts service of process during business hours, and maintains a registered agent. However, for a sterile medical device manufacturer of nitrile examination gloves, the virtual office alone will not satisfy commercial substance requirements under Health Canada's Medical Device Establishment Licence and ISO 13485/MDSAP certification standards; physical production and quality-management facilities are mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate (65% within the first 12 months) given the sterile medical device classification. Health Canada and Alberta regulatory bodies conduct unannounced on-site inspections of manufacturing facilities and quality-control laboratories. The Alberta Corporate Registry may also inspect registered office addresses if service-of-process irregularities arise, and financial institutions' KYC/AML compliance teams may request on-site visits during account opening.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, Part 2 (Limited Partnerships), ss. 51-84, together with the Partnership (Limited Partnership Registration) Regulations; product-level medical device classification is additionally governed by the federal Medical Devices Regulations, SOR/98-282.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, 9925 109 Street NW, Edmonton, Alberta, Canada
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP-01 Registration of Limited Partnership, including Statement of General Partner, Schedule of Limited Partners, and Consent to Act as Registered Office
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Alberta limited partnership; partners must make contributions in cash, property, or services as agreed under the partnership agreement, and the contributions must be recorded in the partnership books maintained at the Alberta registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner approves and adopts the Limited Partnership Agreement of [◆] Alberta Limited Partnership (the 'Partnership'), together with the capital subscription schedule set forth in Schedule A thereto; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Partnership be fixed at [◆], Alberta, Canada, and that [◆] be appointed as registered office representative under the Partnership Act (Alberta); FURTHER RESOLVED, that [◆] be appointed General Partner Representative, with authority to execute and file Form LP-01, engage legal and tax counsel, open banking and payment rail accounts (SWIFT/LC and TT), and obtain all statutory licenses; FURTHER RESOLVED, that all actions of the General Partner Representative in completing the statutory incorporation and governance filings are hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / NUANS Search System via an authorized Service Alberta registry agent or online at albertacorporateinteract.com
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS preliminary name search for the proposed limited partnership name. Request a Name Search Report that includes the proposed distinctive element and legal element ('Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.'). If desired, reserve the approved name for up to 90 days to lock availability prior to registration.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search request form
Three proposed name options with distinctive elements
Signed authorization from the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries or rejects the name for similarity or prohibited terms, submit revised distinctive elements with a fresh NUANS report, or file an appeal with the Registry and respond to the Deficiency Notice within the prescribed response period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement and Capital Contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private notarial execution; if the general partner is a foreign entity, execution must be notarized in the jurisdiction of formation and legalized for Canadian acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the limited partnership agreement defining capital contributions, profit and loss allocations, management authority of the general partner, transfer restrictions, and dissolution triggers. Ensure that the corporate general partner has obtained its own board authorization and that contributions are received into a dedicated partnership account prior to registration, as non-resident ownership is permitted.
required_dossiers: Limited Partnership Agreement
Schedule A of capital contributions
Certificate of good standing or equivalent corporate authorization for corporate general partner
Notarized execution pages and powers of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the executed agreement is rejected on legalizability or signature validity grounds, cure by re-execution before a notary public or commissioner for oaths, and submit an acknowledgement affidavit to the registry or financial institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Registration of the Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta; electronic filing through Alberta Corporate Registration system (ACR) or paper filing at the Edmonton/Calgary offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form LP-01 with the Alberta Corporate Registry, including the registered office address within Alberta, the name and address of the general partner, the names of limited partners, and the amount of contribution of each limited partner. Pay the prescribed registration fee and receive the Certificate of Registration. The partnership is constituted under s. 52 of the Partnership Act upon issuance of the certificate.
required_dossiers: Form LP-01 Registration of Limited Partnership
NUANS Name Search Report
Consent to Act as Registered Office signed by the registered office provider
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Proof of general partner authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a Query Letter, file a Statement of Correction or provide the requested particulars within 60 days; late filings are subject to penalty, and the registration can be retroactively reinstated if the cure is accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Tax Registration and Key Business Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Business Registration Online (BRO) portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership with the CRA to obtain a Business Number, GST/HST account, payroll account, and import/export (RZ) account. Although the partnership is a pass-through entity, the general partner must report partnership income; non-resident limited partners must provide their tax identification details and the partnership must appoint a representative for service of process under the Excise Tax Act where applicable.
required_dossiers: CRA Business Registration Online form RC1
Certificate of Registration of the limited partnership
Particulars of partners and their residency status
Bank account confirmation for GST/HST refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA flags the application for missing partner information, respond to the RR (Request for Information) letter within 30 days with corrected partner schedules; effective dates can be adjusted retroactively to the date of registration upon proof of qualification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Development Permit and Building Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Applicable Alberta municipality (e.g., City of Calgary or City of Edmonton Planning and Development Department); safety codes officers under the Safety Codes Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a development permit for industrial/manufacturing use of the proposed dipping plant site. Submit construction documents for a building permit under the Alberta Building Code, including structural load certifications, fire separation plans, ventilation design for VOC control, and plumbing for industrial wastewater. Obtain a certificate of occupancy before mechanical start-up of dipping lines.
required_dossiers: Development permit application with site plan
Building permit application and architectural/engineering drawings
Structural load and fire safety compliance reports
Industrial wastewater and ventilation system schematics
Land title and zoning certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality or safety codes officer issues deficiencies, resubmit revised drawings and undergo re-inspection; an unsuccessful appeal may be taken to the Alberta Safety Codes Appeal Board in accordance with the Safety Codes Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA); Health Canada, Medical Devices Directorate; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the EPEA Registration for industrial wastewater and air emissions from the dipping and curing process. Apply to Health Canada for a Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) enabling the manufacture and distribution of sterile examination gloves as Class II medical devices. Obtain OHS clearance covering hazardous chemical management (nitrile compounding agents, coagulants, and curing accelerators), emergency response, and worker exposure controls before commencing production.
required_dossiers: EPEA Registration form and process flow diagram
Wastewater and air emission characterization data
Health Canada MDEL application (Form 001) and quality system certificate
OHS hazard assessment and chemical inventory
Fire safety plan and emergency response procedures
Proof of municipal occupancy permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEPA issues an information request or non-compliance notice, submit supplementary monitoring data and a corrective action plan; for MDEL, respond to the Health Canada Deficiency Letter within the stated time window; for OHS orders, remedy the enumerated hazards and file a notice of compliance for re-inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA); Health Canada Medical Devices Directorate; Technical Safety Authority of Alberta (safety codes administration)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: EPEA Industrial Registration/Approval for the manufacturing facility, Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL), and Alberta municipal business/occupancy permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA), Government of Alberta
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration-level screening under the Activities Designation Regulation (AEP) for an industrial chemical dipping facility; a full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is not automatically required for this scale of glove manufacturing, but higher-risk chemical throughput or sensitive-zone siting may elevate the project to an Environmental Assessment screening.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must meet the Alberta Wastewater and Storm Drainage Regulation (pH 6.5-9.0, TSS, BOD5, ammonia, and oil/grease limits); air emissions must comply with Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives (AAAQO) for total VOCs, with specific capture and control on curing ovens; hazardous solid waste from nitrile compounding and wash-water sludge must be manifested and disposed under the Hazardous Waste Regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code (Safety Codes Act) including sprinkler and fire alarm acceptance testing; structural load inspection certificate under the Alberta Building Code for the dipping line and curing oven; occupational workplace clearance from Alberta OHS covering chemical exposure limits, ventilation arrestment, WHMIS training, personal protective equipment, and emergency rescue procedures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); primary portal is CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) at canada.ca/business-registration-online. Alberta corporate income tax is administered on behalf of Alberta by the CRA under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act through the federal Tax Collection Agreement; Alberta has no provincial sales tax and no separate tax registration for limited partnerships. The Alberta LP must also be registered with the Alberta Corporate Registry under the Partnerships Act, and municipal business licensing may apply at the place of operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine GST/HST registration duty under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (ETA). A non-resident Alberta LP carrying on business in Canada must register once its worldwide taxable supplies (exclusive of zero-rated supplies) exceed CAD 30,000 in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters and the current calendar quarter; non-resident fulfillment-warehouse vendors and digital platform sellers delivering goods located in Canada to Canadian recipients must register without any threshold. Step 2: Obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) for the LP via CRA's Business Registration Online, by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) by mail or fax to the Sudbury Tax Centre, or by calling the CRA Business Window; the BN is the statutory TIN and is supplemented by program accounts: RT for GST/HST and RM for import/export accounts. Step 3: File the T5013 Partnership Information Return for the LP's fiscal period where the LP is a Canadian-resident partnership, carries on business in Canada, or has a Canadian-resident partner or a partner required to file a Canadian return; each partner separately reports its allocable share under section 96 of the Income Tax Act. Step 4: Register for an RP payroll account if the LP employs individuals in Canada and obtain a customs RM account for the export declaration obligations. Step 5: Foreign partners with Canadian-source income should obtain their own BN and program accounts when filing Canadian returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — An Alberta limited partnership is fiscally transparent for Canadian tax purposes: income and losses are computed at the partnership level and allocated to partners under section 96 of the Income Tax Act; the LP itself is not subject to federal or Alberta income tax and files only an information return. Non-resident partners are taxable in Canada only on their allocable share of Canadian-source income, subject to treaty relief. The LP is not a 'per se corporation' for US check-the-box purposes and may be treated as a disregarded entity or partnership as elected by its US partners.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The LP is tax-transparent and no entity-level corporate election exists under Canadian law. Relevant statutory elections include: (i) partnership fiscal-period election under ITA s. 249.1(9) permitting a non-calendar year-end in limited circumstances; (ii) GST/HST 'designated member' election pursuant to ETA s. 273 as applied to partnerships, allowing one general partner to account for and remit GST/HST on behalf of the partnership; (iii) election under ETA s. 156 for closely related corporations, relevant only if corporate partners establish a GST/HST group; (iv) election under ITA s. 216 by a non-resident partner to file on a net basis for Canadian rental income; (v) for US partners, reliance on Article IV(6) of the Canada-US Tax Convention to claim treaty benefits through the fiscally transparent LP; and (vi) voluntary GST/HST registration under ETA s. 240(2) when the small-supplier threshold is not exceeded, to claim input tax credits.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax); Alberta applies only the 5% federal GST with no provincial component, and no Alberta retail sales tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated supplies) over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters and the current quarter (the small-supplier threshold); non-resident fulfillment-warehouse vendors and platform sellers supplying goods located in Canada to Canadian recipients are subject to mandatory GST/HST registration with no threshold; non-residents making taxable supplies of real property in Canada are also required to register regardless of revenue.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoice clearance, or digital stamping. E-invoicing is voluntary; the Pan-Canadian Peppol eDelivery Network (PINT/EN 16931) is supported for B2B exchange, and federal government procurement via CanadaBuys expects Peppol-compliant e-invoices. GST/HST tax invoices must be issued on request and contain supplier name, BN, date, description, consideration, and tax amount. Export declarations to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) must be transmitted electronically via the Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED) or a CBSA-approved service provider/API, and all GST/HST records must be retained for six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of sterile examination nitrile gloves qualify for the 0% GST/HST rate under Part V of Schedule VI to the ETA (section 1 for goods exported as soon as is reasonable after sale; section 2 for goods delivered to a common carrier for export; section 3 for goods supplied to a consignee located outside Canada). The exporter must maintain documentary proof of export, generally showing the goods left Canada within 60 days of the sale for direct shipments or within one year for goods moved through bonded or consignment processes. Offshore services rendered to non-residents may be zero-rated under section 7 of Part V if the services relate to goods outside Canada or are otherwise performed for a non-resident and not in connection with Canadian real property. Domestic supplies of qualifying surgical or examination gloves may additionally be zero-rated under Part II of Schedule VI (medical devices) where the goods meet the prescribed description; an advance ruling from the CRA is recommended. Zero-rated exports are taxable supplies at 0%, preserving full input tax credit recovery.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A) filed via the Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED) or the CBSA Export Declaration (G16/G17), or the Carrier Export Declaration (CED) for goods shipped by air or sea
Transport documentation: ocean Bill of Lading or air waybill, including through/inland bills of lading covering movement from Alberta to the foreign destination
Commercial invoice and packing list identifying buyer, seller, Incoterms, quantity, value, and HS classification (e.g., HS 4015.12 for rubber medical gloves), marked as an export sale
CBSA cargo control documents, customs entry/export summary, container tracking receipts, terminal or warehouse receipts, and insurance certificates evidencing physical removal from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, or TT wire credit advice evidencing settlement by the foreign buyer; bank statements showing receipt of foreign currency
Transactional correspondence: purchase order, sales contract, letter of credit (Swift LC) documentation, and any broker's export report demonstrating the foreign destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA audits zero-rating evidence under GST/HST Memorandum 4.4.2 and may reassess within four years of the reporting period, or indefinitely where misrepresentation, fraud, or neglect is established. Deficient export proof causes the supply to be re-characterized as taxable at 5%, resulting in assessment of unpaid GST, interest, and clawback of related input tax credits. Civil penalties under ETA s. 280 apply for false statements or omissions: 5% of the net tax understated, increasing to 25% for willful default, gross negligence, or knowing participation; subsequent violations attract a penalty of CAD 100 or 25% of the claim, whichever is greater. Willful evasion is a criminal offense under ETA s. 327 punishable by fine up to CAD 200,000 and imprisonment up to five years on summary conviction, or up to 200% of the evaded amount on indictment; partners may be liable under ETA ss. 323 and 324, and the federal general anti-avoidance rule may apply to artificial transactions designed to manufacture export refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a fully convertible currency regime under the Bank of Canada Act and foreign exchange regulations enforced by the Department of Finance. Both capital and current accounts are freely convertible with no prior approval requirements for Alberta Limited Partnerships. Profit remittances to foreign partners are permitted without surrender or repatriation mandates, subject only to tax filing obligations and beneficial ownership reporting to the Canada Revenue Agency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement exists for surrender of export proceeds. Canadian exporters may retain foreign currency receipts and convert them at prevailing market rates. All export transactions must be reported to the Canada Border Services Agency and Canada Revenue Agency for statistical and tax purposes. No mandatory conversion timeline or ratio applies; proceeds may be held in foreign currency accounts or converted as needed.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI platforms face significant regulatory constraints under Canadian AML and FATF compliance standards. Corporate entities must route cross-border flows through traditional correspondent banking networks; fintech EMI services are generally not viable for medical PPE supply chain transactions without full bank partnership.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote KYC and account opening is permitted for Alberta Limited Partnerships through video verification and digital document submission. Directors may be required to attend a physical branch interview for enhanced due diligence when transaction volumes exceed CAD 10,000 or when cross-border ownership structures are involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Limited Partnership, partnership agreement, beneficial ownership register, and source-of-funds documentation for any foreign partners or ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Supply chain exposure to high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier due diligence reports, import licenses, and verified transaction history to demonstrate compliance with sanctions and anti-money laundering controls.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions must be received via SWIFT MT103 wire transfers using purpose code 'Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Injection'. Verification requires supporting documentation including partnership agreement, capital contribution resolution, and bank statements. All funds are to be routed through Canadian dollar or CAD-equivalent accounts with full exchange control reporting to the Bank of Canada.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements are cleared primarily through SWIFT MT103. Commercial Letters of Credit are available via correspondent banks. Payments for imported raw materials or PPE components require purpose codes 'Trade Payment' or 'Import Settlement'. All transactions must be supported by matching trade documents, invoices, and proof of goods receipt.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta), Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each annual registration anniversary (recurring calendar event)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No legislated late fee; continued non-filing triggers administrative cancellation of the LP registration. Once cancelled, carrying on business exposes general partners to unlimited liability; reinstatement requires formal restoration and prescribed registry fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (including T5013 Summary)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Calgary Tax Centre
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 5 months after fiscal period end (May 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Income Tax Act s. 162(8) penalty: C$25 per day (minimum C$100) up to C$2,500; electronic filing mandatory for partnerships with 11 or more partners; gross negligence exposure for knowing omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Each partner (primary recipient); CRA (copy attached to T5013 return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following the calendar year of the fiscal period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Income Tax Act s. 162(7): C$25 per missing slip, minimum C$100, maximum C$2,500; additional penalty up to C$1,000 for failure to file the T5013 Summary.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statement of Change (amendment for partner changes, general partner changes, name, or address for service)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days of any registrable change (event-driven, not strictly annual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry particulars become inaccurate; service of process may be ineffective; courts may disregard the limited-liability shield for obligations incurred after the unreported change.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Return (annual filing election or periodic returns with year-end reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers: within 3 months after fiscal year-end (March 31 for December 31 year-end); monthly or quarterly filers: by the end of the following reporting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 1% of unremitted net tax plus 0.25% per full month (maximum 12 months); daily CRA prescribed interest; repeated non-compliance may lead to registration revocation and partner liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None by statute for an Alberta Limited Partnership. An independent audit becomes compulsory only if (i) the LP is a reporting issuer under Canadian provincial securities law, (ii) the partnership agreement or lender covenants impose an audit condition, or (iii) a corporate general partner's own statutory audit obligations consolidate the LP.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: CPA Canada Handbook: IFRS (Part I) for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Part II) for private enterprises; partnership income computed under the federal Income Tax Act with capital cost allowance elections.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta's ISC/UBO transparency regime under the Business Corporations Act applies only to Alberta corporations; limited partnerships file no separate annual UBO declaration. The LP Annual Return confirms the registered general partner; any transfer of partnership interests or change of general partner is evidenced by a Statement of Change filed within 15 days and mirrored in the internal Register of Partners.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (capital contributions and interest-transfer ledger)
Original Statement of Registration, Annual Returns and Statements of Change
Partnership agreement and all amendments and partner resolutions
Registered office, agent, and service-of-process records

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined (15% federal Part I + 8% Alberta) at the corporate-partner level; the Limited Partnership itself is fiscally transparent under the Income Tax Act and bears no entity-level tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED investment tax credits (15% federal non-refundable; 30% refundable for eligible CCPCs); Accelerated Investment Incentive (50% first-year CCA on manufacturing and processing equipment); Alberta flat 8% general rate; reduced 11% combined CCPC small-business rate (9% federal + 2% Alberta) on the first CA$500,000 of active business income if a corporate partner qualifies as a CCPC.
